antidotes.why: The wish to understand answers the weariness that the texts treat as a door.
Not losing heart is the root of fortune.
We act only when we find joy; find where the joy is.

chains.summary: Wherever there is craving, the round of the world is there. The list of things done and not done has never ended for anyone. Everyone suffers from straining, and no one sees it.
chains.title: Where craving is, the round is

verses.m: Everyone is miserable from straining after things, and no one realises it. By this single teaching the fortunate one finds peace.
verses.sa: आयासात्सकलो दुःखी नैनं जानाति कश्चन । अनेनैवोपदेशेन धन्यः प्राप्नोति निर्वृतिम् ॥

depicts.m: Enough of wealth, of desire, even of good deeds. In this wilderness of life the mind never found rest in them.
depicts.sa: अलमर्थेन कामेन सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा । एभ्यः संसारकान्तारे न विश्रान्तमभून् मनः ॥
depicts.why: Shows the weariness of having had wealth, pleasure and merit and found no rest in any.

depicts.m: I somehow put up with the taunts of the wicked while trying to please them; I held back my tears and laughed with an empty heart; I folded my hands even before people whose minds were numbed by money. Hope, futile hope, how much more will you make me dance?
depicts.sa: खलालापाः सोढाः कथमपि तदाराधनपरैः निगृह्यान्तर्बाष्पं हसितमपि शून्येन मनसा । कृतो वित्तस्तम्भप्रतिहतधियामञ्जलिरपि त्वमाशे मोघाशे किमपरमतो नर्तयसि माम् ॥
depicts.why: Depicts laughing with an empty heart.

depicts.m: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
depicts.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
depicts.sa: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
depicts.why: Shows the thought itself: I keep working and nothing comes of it.

depicts.m: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
depicts.sa: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥
depicts.why: Shows everything studied and not filled.

depicts.r: Complete Works, Vol. 6, Notes of Class Talks and Lectures: On Bhakti-Yoga, p. 91
depicts.sa: Lord! I have become weary. Oh, take me by the hand, Lord, I take shelter with Thee
depicts.why: Gives wanting nothing of this world or another.

depicts.m: I dug up the earth hoping for treasure, smelted the ores of mountains, crossed the ocean, lord of rivers, worked hard to please kings, spent nights in cremation grounds with my mind fixed on mantras, and I did not get even a broken cowrie. Craving, be satisfied now!
depicts.sa: उत्खातं निधिशङ्कया क्षितितलं ध्माता गिरेर्धातवो निस्तीर्णः सरितां पतिर्नृपतयो यत्नेन संतोषिताः । मन्त्राराधनतत्परेण मनसा नीताः श्मशाने निशाः प्राप्तः काणवराटकोऽपि न मया तृष्णे सकामा भव ॥

depicts.m: Thinking 'it is the same night again, the same day', creatures run about in vain, busy as ever with the tasks they have set going; with work full of the same repeated things, tormented by this round of existence, alas, out of delusion we feel no shame.
depicts.sa: रात्रिः सैव पुनः स एव दिवसो मत्वा मुधा जन्तवो धावन्त्युद्यमिनस्तथैव निभृतप्रारब्धतत्तत्क्रियाः । व्यापारैः पुनरुक्तभूत विषयैरित्थंविधेनामुना संसारेण कदर्थिता वयमहो मोहान्न लज्जामहे ॥
depicts.why: Names the sameness of days, said from inside.

depicts.m: So no peace came into our minds, Lord. We have come to your world and taken refuge in you.
depicts.sa: अतो नेवाभवच्छान्तिरस्माकं चेतसि प्रभो!। वयं शरणमापन्ना भवल्लोकमुपस्थिताः ॥

gloss: Having no taste left for what one was doing. In Valmiki it is losing heart. In the Mundaka and Gita 2.52 the same weariness is the turn toward seeking.

heals.m: The infinite alone is happiness; there is no happiness in the small. The infinite alone is happiness. So the infinite must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand the infinite.'
heals.sa: यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति भूमैव सुखं भूमा त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्य इति भूमानं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
heals.why: Names emptiness as getting small things leads to emptiness.

heals.m: He understood that joy is Brahman. From joy these beings are born, by joy they live once born, and into joy they enter at death. This is the wisdom of Bhrigu and Varuna, established in the highest space. Whoever knows this becomes established.
heals.sa: आनन्दो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात्। आनन्दाध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । आनन्देन जातानि जीवन्ति । आनन्दं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । सैषा भार्गवी वारुणी विद्या । परमे व्योमन्प्रतिष्ठिता ।स य एवं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति ।
heals.why: Shows existence resting on joy from start to end, however flat it feels now.

heals.m: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
heals.sa: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
heals.why: Shows weariness is refused a verdict.

heals.m: How can a person who lives and works in the middle of the world not be bound by it, the way water sits on a lotus leaf?
heals.sa: संसार एव निवहे जनो व्यवहरन्नपि । न बन्धं कथमाप्नोति पद्मपत्रे पयो यथा ॥

heals.m: There is nothing higher than me, Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me like pearls on a thread.
heals.sa: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥

heals.m: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
heals.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
heals.sa: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
heals.why: Names both possible ends of unrewarded work.

heals.m: There is no duty equal to doing good to others, brother, and no baseness equal to causing others pain. This is the verdict of all the scriptures; the wise know it.
heals.sa: पर हित सरिस धर्म नहिं भाई। पर पीड़ा सम नहिं अधमाई॥ निर्नय सकल पुरान बेद कर। कहेउँ तात जानहिं कोबिद नर ॥
heals.why: Heals by giving a purpose that needs no special station.

heals.m: Without devotion, all virtues and pleasures are like many dishes without salt. What use is happiness without devotion? Thinking so, I spoke.
heals.sa: भगति हीन गुन सब सुख ऐसे। लवन बिना बहु बिंजन जैसे॥ भजन हीन सुख कवने काजा। अस बिचारि बोलेउँ खगराजा ॥
heals.why: Shows the full life that still tastes flat is given a reason.

hero.m: Know that to be yoga: the breaking of contact with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and with an undespairing mind.
hero.sa: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥

loci.m: Know that to be yoga: the breaking of contact with sorrow. This yoga should be practised with determination and with an undespairing mind.
loci.sa: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम् । स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ॥

practices.m: Do not stir your mind with yes and no, with plans and doubts. Be still, and rest happily in your own joyful Self.
practices.sa: मा सङ्कल्पविकल्पाभ्यां चित्तं क्षोभय चिन्मय । उपशाम्य सुखं तिष्ठ स्वात्मन्यानन्दविग्रहे ॥
practices.why: Shows the self is called ananda-vigraha.

practices.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
practices.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
practices.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥

practices.m: The ear is beautiful through learning, not earrings; the hand through giving, not bracelets; the body of the compassionate shines through helping others, not through sandal paste.
practices.sa: श्रोत्रं श्रुतेनैव न कुण्डलेन दानेन पाणिर्न तु कङ्कणेन । विभाति कायः करुणापराणां परोपकारैर्न तु चन्दनेन ॥
practices.why: Shows the body shining by helping.

practices.m: If an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself over it. Keep applying yourself again and again; this is the highest rule for those who lead.
practices.sa: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः
practices.why: Shows renewed exertion is called the supreme rule.

practices.m: To bear no ill will toward any being in deed, thought or word, to help, and to give: this is the timeless way of the good.
practices.sa: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा / अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः

practices.m: Whether he wins or fails, the wise person does not keep grieving. He starts on the next task at once and does not hoard his own life.
practices.sa: अलब्ध्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः / आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते
practices.why: Shows starting what comes next immediately.

stories.l: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
stories.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
stories.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root

stories.l: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
stories.s: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
stories.t: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf

stories.l: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.
stories.s: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
stories.t: Do right without reward, and keep working

stories.l: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.
stories.s: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.
